root_cause.text: The credit check in virtio_transport_inc_rx_pkt() only accounts for payload length (rx_bytes) and not the per-skb metadata overhead, so zero-length packets with VIRTIO_VSOCK_SEQ_EOM can bypass the limit and cause unbounded queue growth.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description states that "virtio_transport_inc_rx_pkt() checks vvs->rx_bytes + len > vvs->buf_alloc" and "if fed with packets with len == 0 and VIRTIO_VSOCK_SEQ_EOM, a very large number of packets can be queued because vvs->rx_bytes stays at 0"; the fix adds an estimate of skb overhead using SKB_TRUESIZE(0) multiplied by queue length.

intent_record.what: Added a variable skb_overhead computed as (rx_queue length + 1) * SKB_TRUESIZE(0) and included it in the buffer usage check.
intent_record.how: The condition now accounts for the memory overhead of SKB structures, preventing the receiver from exceeding its buffer allocation by considering both data and SKB overhead.
